notes: source.mutex.guard.v1 with card T03-F's `wait NAME;` form: a child task announces an acquisition it never performs, and the generation's destruction at scope exit is refused at Q619 NonquiescentMutexDestruction. The exact ordered cascade [Q619, Q600 NonquiescentDestruction, Q600 OutstandingMutex, Q600 OutstandingWaiter] is pinned, and every entry after the first is load-bearing: the refused destruction must leave the generation live, must therefore also refuse the protected resource's destruction, and must still name the mutex and the outstanding waiter in the end-of-trace sweep. A cascade that ended after Q619 would mean the refusal had quietly destroyed something anyway. RegisterWaiter existed in the checker with no source form before T03-F, which is exactly why this case was unmappable; the waiter half is now reached from source. The performed.qr control has the announcing task perform the acquisition, which withdraws the announcement, and is accepted — so Q619 is keyed to the outstanding announcement and not to a child task naming a mutex. Only parser and type_checker execute on the case artifact; cfg is unassessed because this route has no CFG stage. NOT established: any native evidence. `wait m;` is deliberately in the emission-refused set (an announced acquisition only another thread could satisfy has no honest single-thread rendering), so the accepted control is published checked with c_source: None; evidence_target=linux records host gating by the Q500 target refusal, not a compiled or executed run. This is the model's waiter bookkeeping, not a blocking-acquisition or deadlock claim.
